lead: Bootstrap is a CSS framework: a ready-made CSS file plus a JavaScript bundle that gives you a reset, a 12-column grid, components and utility classes. Instead of writing new CSS for every page, you assemble the page from class names such as container, row, col-md-6, card and m-3. This saves time and keeps spacing consistent across a team. It is used for admin dashboards, college portals, landing pages and prototypes, where a responsive layout is needed quickly. The same idea appears in Tailwind, Bulma, Foundation and Materialize.
prereq: You need: selectors and the cascade from 2.5, the box model from 2.6, colour and type from 2.7, and Flexbox plus media queries from 2.8.

sections.h3: What a framework supplies and the 12-column grid

blocks.text: Bootstrap is a CSS framework: one CSS file plus one JavaScript bundle. The CSS file supplies four things. A reset (Bootstrap calls it Reboot) removes browser default differences. A grid places content in rows and columns. Components are finished blocks such as buttons and navbars. Utilities are single-purpose classes such as m-3 for margin. The JavaScript bundle adds behaviour to components that need it, such as a modal opening. You use the framework by writing class names in HTML, not by writing new CSS for each page.

The grid has three levels. container is a centred wrapper with a maximum width; container-fluid spans the full viewport width. Inside it, row is a flex container with negative side margins. Inside the row, every col-* is a flex item with side padding. The padding and negative margin form the gutter, the space between columns. A row holds 12 column units.

blocks.where: W is the row content width in pixels (960 px in the worked example); s is the span in column units, from 1 to 12. These widths ignore the gutter; treat them as the share of the row taken by each column.

blocks.text: Three col-4 columns fill the row because 4 + 4 + 4 = 12.

Breakpoints make the grid responsive. Bootstrap defines sm 576 px, md 768 px, lg 992 px, xl 1200 px and, from version 5, xxl 1400 px. A class such as col-md-4 means: from 768 px upward, this column spans 4 units. Below 768 px it takes the full row width and stacks. The suffix is a minimum, not an exact width; col-md-4 still applies at 1000 px and at 1400 px unless a larger suffix overrides it. A row with spans that total more than 12 does not shrink its columns. Bootstrap uses flex wrapping, so extra columns move to the next line. A row of three col-md-6 has spans 6 + 6 + 6 = 18, so the first two sit side by side and the third wraps. Always keep col-* inside row, and row inside a container. Putting a column straight inside a container loses the row's flex context and gutter alignment.

Components are named blocks: navbar for the top menu, card for a boxed item, btn for buttons, form-control for input, alert for a message and modal for a dialog. Utilities set one property: m-3 sets margin on all sides to spacing step 3, p-2 sets padding step 2, text-center centres text and d-flex turns the element into a flex container. The spacing number is a scale step, not a pixel count. Version 4 needs jQuery for its JavaScript components and uses ml/mr for left/right margin. Version 5 drops jQuery, uses ms/me (start/end) and adds the xxl breakpoint. You can load the compiled files from a CDN or copy bootstrap.min.css and bootstrap.bundle.min.js into your project. To change colours, spacing or breakpoints before compiling, override Sass variables. Other frameworks follow the same idea: Tailwind is utility-first, Bulma is class-based without JavaScript, Foundation is configurable, and Materialize follows Material Design. Deep Sass build setups with npm belong to Unit 6.

figure.caption: Each cell is one column and its number is the width in pixels on the 960 px row, where one of the 12 units is 80 px: row A gives three 320 px columns, row B gives 640 px and 320 px. The last row shows three 6-wide columns, whose spans total 18, so the third 480 px column wraps to a new line instead of shrinking.

spec.title: One 960 px row = 12 units of 80 px
spec.aria: Four Bootstrap rows on a 960 px content width, with column widths in pixels: row A has three 4-span columns of 320 px each, row B has an 8-span column of 640 px beside a 4-span column of 320 px, row C is a single 12-span column of 960 px, and a last row of three 6-span columns of 480 px each totals 18 spans so the third column wraps to a new line.

examples.question: A Bootstrap row has a content width of 960 px; ignore the gutter. Row A holds three col-md-4 columns. Row B holds col-md-8 and col-md-4. Row C holds one col-12. Find the width of every column in pixels. Then a designer replaces Row A with three col-md-6 columns: find the total span and say what Bootstrap does.
steps: Row A: each col-md-4 has span 4, so width = 80 × 4 = 320 px. Three columns give 3 × 320 = 960 px.
Row B: col-md-8 is 80 × 8 = 640 px; col-md-4 is 320 px. Sum = 640 + 320 = 960 px.
Three col-md-6 columns have spans 6 + 6 + 6 = 18. 18 is greater than 12, so Bootstrap does not shrink them; it wraps the third column to a new line. The first line then holds two columns.
examples.answer: Row A: 320 px, 320 px, 320 px; Row B: 640 px and 320 px; Row C: 960 px. Three col-md-6 total 18 spans, so the third wraps.
examples.check:
row = 960
unit = row / 12
for span in (4, 4, 4, 8, 4, 12):
    print(int(unit * span))
print(6 + 6 + 6)

traps: Putting a col-* directly inside a container with no row between: without the row there is no flex container and no negative margins, so the gutter padding disappears and the columns no longer line up beside each other as intended.
Expecting columns to shrink when spans exceed 12: Bootstrap wraps the extra column to the next line; it does not divide 12 again.
Using Bootstrap 4 spacing classes in version 5: ml-3/mr-3 become ms-3/me-3, and version 5 does not load jQuery for components.
Reading col-md-4 as a class only at exactly 768 px: it applies from 768 px upward; below that the column is full width.
Treating m-3 as 3 px: it is one step on the spacing scale, not a pixel value.

quiz.q: List the four things a CSS framework such as Bootstrap supplies.
quiz.a: A reset/base style, a grid, components and utilities; it also ships JavaScript behaviour for some components.

quiz.q: Why should a col-* live inside a row rather than directly inside a container?
quiz.a: The row is the flex container and supplies the negative margins that form gutters. Columns supply matching padding. Without the row, the flex context and gutter alignment are lost.

quiz.q: A container content width is 1200 px. A row has col-lg-3 and col-lg-9. Find each column width.
quiz.a: One unit is 1200 ÷ 12 = 100 px. col-lg-3 is 100 × 3 = 300 px; col-lg-9 is 100 × 9 = 900 px; total 1200 px.

quiz.q: A 960 px row has three col-md-5 columns. Give each width and say what happens.
quiz.a: One unit is 80 px; each column is 80 × 5 = 400 px. Spans total 5 + 5 + 5 = 15, so the first two sit side by side and the third wraps to a new line.

quiz.q: A page built on Bootstrap 4 uses ml-3 and a modal. It is moved to Bootstrap 5 without changes. Name two likely problems.
quiz.a: ml-3 is not a version 5 class; use ms-3. Code that relied on jQuery for the modal may break because version 5 components do not use jQuery.

quiz.q: A student writes <div class="container"> <div class="col-md-6">A</div> <div class="col-md-6">B</div> </div>. Predict the layout and fix it.
quiz.a: The columns sit directly in the container with no row, so they lose the row's flex context and gutter padding and no longer share a line. Wrap both columns in a <div class="row"> inside the container.

quiz.q: What does col-md-4 mean at 600 px and at 900 px?
quiz.a: At 600 px it is below the md breakpoint, so the column takes the full row width. At 900 px it spans 4 of 12 units, one-third of the row.

beyond: Not for the exam. In industry, teams often combine a framework with design tokens and a build step, so one Sass file or CSS variable set controls colours, spacing and dark mode. Utility-first CSS, seen in Tailwind, has shifted many projects from component classes to small atomic classes. Component libraries add framework classes to React or Angular components; see Unit 5 for React and Angular. Newer CSS features such as container queries and cascade layers reduce the need for some framework helpers. Search next for Bootstrap grid examples, Sass variable overrides, and utility-first CSS comparisons.
